questions: Which side of the heart pumps to the body?
Which side pumps to the lungs?
segments.say: The heart is a double pump. Watch the two blood dots: the left side pushes oxygen-rich blood to the body, the right side pushes oxygen-poor blood to the lungs. Point at each side on your student notes diagram as it pumps.

questions: How many times does blood pass through the heart in one circuit?
segments.say: Two loops: heart to lungs, heart to body. Trace the pulmonary loop as it loads oxygen, then the systemic loop as it delivers oxygen. Blood passes through the heart twice - a double circulation. Now try the loops question on your worksheet.

questions: Which tissue lifts water, and from where?
Which tissue shares food, and from where?
segments.say: Xylem lifts water; phloem shares food. Plants move materials with no heart at all: xylem carries water and minerals up from the soil, phloem moves food from the leaves to wherever it is needed.

questions: What blood does the pulmonary artery carry?
Why is it still an artery?
segments.say: A common mistake: arteries always carry oxygen. Follow the pulmonary artery to the lungs and judge it by direction, not colour. Before we finish, work through the trap section of your student notes in pairs, check the worksheet answers, then do the exit ticket on your own.
segments.watchFor: Arteries always carry oxygenated blood. Listen for students who colour every artery red or call the pulmonary artery a vein. Send them back to scene 2: The pulmonary artery is the exception: it carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
